about: Posts built on other posts. When a source post changes, the posts built on it are brought in line with it: the lane that changes the source carries the change over, or puts it to Joel, in the same turn. A lane working on a built-on post first checks what changed in its sources since it was last brought in line, so the post is edited once. Each change goes through the humanization rules of the post it lands in: a changed paragraph is checked by itself and goes in only at Human High (tools/humanization/apply_gate.py); his own words go to him; the post on Substack is updated only with his yes (gate E323). A paragraph that reads Human High now and would only gain a fact may be better left with a link to the source than rewritten. docs/FIXING-AN-ARTICLE.md (section 1, item 6) gives the steps; tools/humanization/lane_push.py prints the entries for the article it pushes; ARTICLE-META-MAP.md draws them. This is the BUILT-ON list of the Substack-system lane's design (docs/proposals/2026-11-20-substack-system-HANDOFF.md): extend this file, don't start another.
